Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:1.hebrew: נקדר - הבשר בסכין מעל השבר בעגול כמין טבעת, ורוב הקיפו מכוסה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:1.english: Cut around - [That is,] the flesh [was cut] with a knife from over the break in a circle like a ring, while most of its circumference is [still] covered:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:2.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרינן: כיון דנקדר בעגול, שוב אינו מעלה ארוכה, או לא אמרינן:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Do we say [that] since it was cut in a circle, it will no longer heal, or do we not say [so]:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:3.hebrew: מסרטו בעצם - דעלמא, ומתוך שהוא מוציא דם, מתחבר הבשר ונמשך זה אצל זה ומעלה ארוכה, וכן דרך הרופאים:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:3.english: One makes an incision in it with a bone - [a bone] from elsewhere; and because it draws blood, the flesh joins together and is drawn one [side] to the other, and it heals, and such is the practice of physicians:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:4.english: It causes inflammation - [Iron] makes incisions in the flesh and causes pain to the wound:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:5.hebrew: והוא דקנה גרמא דידיה - שאנו רואים שהעצם מחזיק בשלו סביבות הקדירה, מידבק העצם לבשר, וסימן התחלת עלות ארוכה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:10:5.english: And this is provided that the bone holds onto its [flesh] - [meaning] that we see that the bone is holding onto its own [flesh] around the circular cut, [that] the bone adheres to the flesh, and it is a sign of the beginning of healing:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:1.english: A hearty soul - [meaning] that his mind is not repulsed by it due to disgust:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:2.hebrew: תאכלנה - ולא אמרינן אבר מן החי היא, שגם היא ניתר בשחיטת האם:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:2.english: May eat it - and we do not say [that] it is a limb from a living animal, for it too is permitted through the slaughter of the mother:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:3.english: And it does not become impure - because it is not considered food:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:4.english: Nor the ritual impurity of animal carcasses - [Even] if the animal died:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:5.english: [If] one intended [regarding] it - for eating:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:6.hebrew: מטמאה טומאת אוכלין - אם נגעה בטומאה, דמחשבה משויא ליה אוכל:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:6.english: [It] becomes impure [with] the ritual impurity of food - If it touched ritual impurity, for intention renders it food:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:7.hebrew: אבל לא טומאת נבלות - דלאו בשר הוא, אלא כשאר אוכל בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:11:7.english: But not the ritual impurity of animal carcasses - because it is not meat, rather it is like any other ordinary food:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:12:1.hebrew: אסורה באכילה - ואע"ג דלא נפק אלא פורתא, וליכא למימר כל מיחוי הולד היה שם, שמא באותו מקצת יצא ראש הולד, והרי הוא כילוד:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:12:1.english: [Its] consumption is prohibited - Even though only a small amount emerged, and one cannot say [that] all the dissolved [matter of] the fetus was there, [nonetheless] perhaps the head of the fetus emerged in that part, and behold, it is like [one that has been] born:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:12:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: "סימן ולד באשה וסימן ולד בבהמה":
Rashi on Chullin 77a:12:2.english: This is the reading: "An indication of a fetus in a woman and an indication of a fetus in an animal":

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:1.english: An animal giving birth to its firstborn - this is its first issue of the womb:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:2.hebrew: ישליכנה לכלבים - שאין בה קדושה, דאע"ג דאין שליא בלא ולד, הכא רובה לאו בת מיקדשה היא, דדלמא נקבה הוה, כדלקמן בגמרא:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:2.english: One may cast it to the dogs - For there is no sanctity in it; for although there is no placenta without a fetus, here, the majority [of cases] is not subject to sanctification, for perhaps it was a female, as [explained] below in the Gemara:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:3.english: And in [the case of] consecrated [animals] - such as a peace-offering animal that expelled a placenta:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:4.hebrew: תקבר - דכיון דאין שליא בלא ולד, קדשה; דבין זכר ובין נקבה דנפיק מבהמת הקדש, קדיש:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:4.english: It must be buried - Because since there is no placenta without a fetus, [the placenta] is consecrated; for whether [it is] a male or a female that emerges from a consecrated animal, it is consecrated:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:5.hebrew: בפרשת דרכים - מקום שהדרכים מתפרשים לשנים, ודרך המנחשים לקוברה שם, שלא תפיל עוד:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:5.english: At a crossroads - A place where the roads branch off in two [directions], and it is the practice of diviners to bury it there so that [the animal] will not miscarry again:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:6.hebrew: דרכי האמורי - ניחוש, וכתיב (שמות כג) "ולא תעשה כמעשיהם":
Rashi on Chullin 77a:13:6.english: The ways of the Amorite - [This is] divination, and it is written (Exodus 23[:24]), "And you shall not do according to their deeds":

Rashi on Chullin 77a:15:1.hebrew: למה לי קרא - למימר "ולא שליתה"? פשיטא דאסורה, דשמא יצא הולד והרי הוא כילוד, ושליא בתריה אזלא ולא שריתה שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:15:1.english: Why do I [need] a verse - to say "and not its placenta"? It is obvious that it is forbidden, for perhaps the fetus emerged [from the womb] and is [therefore considered] as having been born, and the placenta follows after it, and [thus] slaughter [of the mother] does not permit it:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:15:2.hebrew: אסמכתא בעלמא - ולדרשא אחריתי אתא עיקר קרא, לחותך מן הטחול ומן הכליות, כדאמר לעיל בפירקין (חולין דף סט.):
Rashi on Chullin 77a:15:2.english: A mere support - And the primary [purpose of the] verse comes for a different exposition: for [the case of] one who cuts from the spleen and from the kidneys, as it stated earlier in our chapter (Chullin 69a):

Rashi on Chullin 77a:16:1.english: A donkey hide - for it is hard and repulsive:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:16:2.english: That one overcooked it - he boiled it very much:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:16:3.english: If [it was] with regard to the ritual impurity of food - whether it becomes food so as to contract the ritual impurity of food:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:1:1.hebrew: נמנין עליהם - דאפי' לא נמנה אדם עם החבורה אלא לאכול מהן, יצא ידי אכילת פסח. אלמא בשר נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:1:1.english: One may be registered on their account - [That is,] even if a person was registered with the group only to eat from them, he has fulfilled the obligation of eating the Paschal offering. Evidently, they are [considered] flesh:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:2:1.hebrew: ר"ל - פליג עליה בפסחים ב"כיצד צולין" (פסחים דף פד.), ואמר: אין נמנין; והכא לאכשורי טרפה קאתי, ואיסורא דאורייתא היא, ואת אמרת כו':
Rashi on Chullin 77a:2:1.english: Reish Lakish - disagrees with him [Rabbi Yochanan] in Pesachim, in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesachim 84a), and says: "One may not be registered [for those sinews]"; and here [this ruling] comes to permit a tereifa, and it is a Torah prohibition, and you say ["What concern is there with them?"], etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:3:1.hebrew: ואמאי אישתיק והאמר רבא - ביבמות בהחולץ: "הלכתא כריש לקיש בהני תלת, ותו לא" — קנין פירות, והחולץ למעוברת, ומתנה באמצע, כולן בהחולץ. אלמא בהך דגידין הרכין, הלכתא כר' יוחנן, דאע"ג דסופן להקשות, הרי הן עכשיו כבשר:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:3:1.english: And why was he silent? But doesn't Rava say - In Yevamot, in [the chapter] HaCholetz, [Rava said]: "The halakha is in accordance with Reish Lakish in these three [matters], and no more" — [namely,] ownership of produce [by a husband], one who performs *chalitzah* with a pregnant woman, and [one who places] a condition in the middle [of a betrothal formula]; all of them are in [chapter] HaCholetz. Thus, in this [case of] soft sinews, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan, [who holds] that even though they will eventually harden, they are now [considered] like meat:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:4:1.hebrew: שאני הכא דהדר ביה ר' יוחנן - מגידין הרכין, ואמר: כל מידי דסופן להקשות, בתר סוף אזלינן; דמעיקרא הוה סמיך ר' יוחנן אהא דתנן בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין קכב.): עור הראש של עגל הרך הוי כבשר לטומאת אוכלין ונבלות, ואע"ג דסופו להקשות, והדר ביה ואוקמה לההיא כיחידאה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:4:1.english: Here it is different, as Rabbi Yochanan retracted - from [his ruling regarding] soft sinews, and said [that for] anything whose end is to harden, we follow [its] end [state]. For originally Rabbi Yochanan relied on that which we learned in [the chapter entitled] HaOr VeHaRotev (below, Chullin 122a): The skin of the head of a young calf is like meat with respect to food impurity and carcass impurity, even though its end is to harden — and [now] he retracted [his position] and established that [Mishnah] as [the view of] an individual [Sage]:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:4:2.hebrew: דאמר ליה - ר' יוחנן לריש לקיש בהעור והרוטב, דקבעי מיניה: עור הראש של עגל הרך, מהו שיטמא? ואמר ליה: אינו מטמא, הואיל וסופו להקשות. ואמר ליה: הרי שנינו "ואלו שעורותיהן כבשרן — עור הראש של עגל הרך"! ואמר ליה: אל תקניטני בה, שבלשון יחיד אני שונה אותה; כלומר, יחידאה היא ולא סבירא לן כוותיה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:4:2.english: As he said to him - Rabbi Yochanan [said] to Reish Lakish in [the chapter] Ha'Or VeHaRotev, where [Reish Lakish] asked him: "Does the skin of the head of a tender calf convey impurity?" And [Rabbi Yochanan] said to him: "It does not convey impurity, since it will eventually harden." And [Reish Lakish] said to him: "Behold, we learned [in a Mishnah]: 'And these [are the things] whose skins are like their flesh: the skin of the head of a tender calf'!" And [Rabbi Yochanan] said to him: "Do not provoke me about it, for I teach it in the singular [i.e., as an individual opinion]"; that is to say, it is an individual opinion and we do not hold in accordance with it.

Rashi on Chullin 77a:5:1.hebrew: דאישתקיל קורטיתא - לשון קורט, כלומר: מעט מן העצם נעכל ונפל לארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:5:1.english: That a kurtita [small piece] was removed - [This is] an expression [related to] koret [a tiny bit], meaning that a small amount of the bone decayed and fell to the ground:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:5:2.english: He delayed it three festivals - to ask [the] halakhah from the Sages who gather for the festival:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:1.hebrew: א"ל רב אדא בר מתנה - לבעל הבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:1.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to him - to the owner of the animal:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:2.english: Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Chama - He is Rava, the disputant of Abaye:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:3.english: Whose knife is sharp - [he has] an open mind in reasoning:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:4.hebrew: מכדי נשבר העצם ויצא לחוץ תנן - בברייתא דלעיל; מה לי נפל מיניה, מה לי איתיה — הואיל ועור ובשר חופין את רובו, כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:6:4.english: Since we learned: "[If] the bone broke and protruded outward" - in the baraita above; what difference is it to me [whether] it fell from it, [and] what difference is it to me [whether] it is [still] there — since skin and flesh cover most of it, [the animal] is kosher:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:7:1.hebrew: מתלקט מהו - בשר הנותר לכסות הרוב אינו יחד, אלא כאן מעט וכאן מעט סביב העצם, ואם תצרפהו, הרי רוב הקיפו נכסה:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:7:1.english: [If it is] gathered, what is [the halakha] - The flesh remaining to cover the majority [of the bone] is not together [in one place], rather [there is] a little here and a little there around the bone, and if you combine it, the majority of its circumference is covered:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:7:2.english: [If it is] pulverized, what is [the halakha]? - [Meaning] that the flesh was flattened and thin, and covers the majority of the bone:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:7:3.english: [It] became decomposed - The flesh that remains to cover [the bone] has rotted:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:7:4.english: Cuts it away [kodro] - [He] removes it with a knife, like cutting out a skylight:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו ניקב - אותו בשר החופה את העצם, נקב קטן בלא חסרון:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them: [If] it was perforated - [meaning] that flesh which covers [the bone] [sustained] a small perforation without any loss [of flesh]:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Does it constitute a defect, or not?

Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:3.hebrew: נקלף מעל העצם - אותו בשר החופה ואינו דבוק בעצם, מהו? את"ל נקלף בלא חסרון הבשר, כשר:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:3.english: Peeled from upon the bone - [Meaning,] that flesh which covers [the bone] and is not attached to the bone — what is [the law]? If you say [that when it is] peeled without any deficiency of the flesh, it is kosher:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:4.english: Was cracked - [If] the flesh remaining for covering [the bone was cracked], what is [the halakha]?

Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:5.hebrew: ניטל שליש התחתון - של עובי הבשר סמוך לעצם, הרי שני שלישי עליונים עומדים באויר, מהו:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:8:5.english: The bottom third was removed - of the thickness of the flesh adjacent to the bone, [such that] the upper two-thirds are standing in the air — what is [the halakha]:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:9:1.hebrew: ת"ש - לפשוט חדא מהנך בעיי: דאמר ר' יוחנן: "עור הרי הוא כבשר", אלמא ניטל שליש התחתון ונשאר העור ושני שלישי עומדים — כל שכן דכשר:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:9:1.english: Come [and] hear - [to resolve] one of those dilemmas: since Rabbi Yochanan said, "Skin is like flesh," it follows that [if] the lower third was removed and the skin remained while two-thirds remain standing, all the more so it is kosher:

Rashi on Chullin 77a:9:2.hebrew: דלמא התם דקנה משכא דידיה - שהחזיק העור בשלו, כלומר: התם לאו בניטל הבשר מתחתיו והעור עומד באויר קאמר, אלא כגון שנשבר העצם בשיפולו, שהוא ערום מבשר סמוך לארכובה, שאין שם אלא עור, והעור דבוק יפה בעצם ומחזיקו:
Rashi on Chullin 77a:9:2.english: Perhaps there [it is a case where] the skin holds its own - [meaning] that the skin has taken hold of its own [place]; that is to say, there [Rabbi Yoḥanan] is not speaking of [a case where] the flesh was removed from beneath it and the skin stands in the air, but rather [of a case] such as where the bone was broken at its lower end — which is bare of flesh, near the knee — where there is nothing there except skin, and the skin is firmly adhered to the bone and holds it [in place]:

Tosafot on Chullin 77a:4:1.hebrew: אל תקניטני - דאותביה ריש לקיש לר' יוחנן מההיא ד"אלו שעורותיהן כבשרן" כו'. וא"ת: לדידיה גופיה תקשה ליה, דהא קסבר דבתר בסוף אזלינן בהך גידין שסופן להקשות! וי"ל: דלא דמי פסח דלאכילה לטומאה, דאפי' עור ששלקו מטמא טומאת אוכלין כיון דחזי לאכילה, כדאמר בסמוך, ואע"ג דודאי אין נמנין עליו בפסח, והכי נמי גידין שסופן להקשות. וכן בפרק כיצד צולין (פסחים פד.) דפריך מההיא דר' יוחנן, דאמר עור הראש של עגל הרך אין מטמא טומאת אוכלין, אההיא דגידין שסופן להקשות — מכ"ש פריך. ובירושלמי אההיא דראשו של עגל הרך: א"ר יוחנן, לא שנו אלא לטומאה, אבל ללקות לא; ור"ל אמר, משנה שלמה היא זו, בין לטומאה ובין ללקות. ומסיק התם: מיחלף שיטתיה דר"ל! תמן לא עביד לה בשר — גבי גידין שסופן להקשות, דאמר אין נמנין — וכאן עביד ליה בשר! א"ר בון: טעמא דריש לקיש — "ואכלו את הבשר", בשר ולא גידין. משמע לפי הירושלמי דבכל מקום אזיל בתר השתא, בר מגבי פסח דכתיב קרא:
Tosafot on Chullin 77a:4:1.english: Do not provoke me - For Reish Lakish challenged Rabbi Yoḥanan from that [Mishnah of] "These are the hides that are like their meat," etc. And if you ask: Against [Reish Lakish] himself it should be a difficulty, for he holds that we follow the end [state] in this [case of] sinews that will eventually harden! One can answer: Pesach, which is for eating, is not comparable to [ritual] impurity; for even a hide that one boiled contracts food impurity since it is fit for eating, as [the Gemara] says nearby, even though one certainly may not be registered on it for the Paschal offering — and so too [with] sinews that will eventually harden. And similarly in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesaḥim 84a), where [the Gemara] challenges from that [statement] of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said [that] the hide of the head of a tender calf does not contract food impurity, against that [statement] regarding sinews that will eventually harden — it challenges by an a fortiori argument. And in the Jerusalem Talmud, regarding that [Mishnah] of the head of a tender calf: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They only taught [this] with respect to impurity, but with respect to lashes, no; whereas Reish Lakish said: This is a complete Mishnah, [applying] both to impurity and to lashes. And [the Jerusalem Talmud] concludes there: The position of Reish Lakish is reversed! There — regarding sinews that will eventually harden, where he says one may not register [on them] — he does not treat them as meat; whereas here, he treats it as meat! Rabbi Bun said: Reish Lakish's reason [is the verse], "And they shall eat the flesh" (Exodus 12:8) — "flesh," and not sinews. It is implied according to the Jerusalem Talmud that everywhere [Reish Lakish] follows the present [state], except regarding the Paschal offering, where a verse is written:

Tosafot on Chullin 77a:4:2.hebrew: בלשון יחיד כו' - היה שונה במשנה "דברי ר"ש", ולא כמו שפי' בקונטרס משום דאתיא כיחידאה; דבפרק החולץ (יבמות דף מב:) פריך: והא א"ר יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה, אע"ג דאתיא כר' יהודה! וא"ת: וממאי דמההיא דפסח הדר ביה, ודלמא מההיא דלקמן הדר ביה? וי"ל: דמסתמא הדר ביה לגבי חבריה:
Tosafot on Chullin 77a:4:2.english: In the singular, etc. - [Rabbi Yoḥanan] would teach [it] in the Mishnah [as] "the words of Rabbi Shimon," and not as Rashi explained, [that he meant] because it follows an individual opinion; for in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 42b), [the Gemara] objects: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say [that] the halakha is in accordance with an anonymous Mishnah, even though it follows Rabbi Yehuda! And if you say: From what [do we know] that he retracted from that [ruling] regarding the Passover [offering] — perhaps he retracted from that [ruling] later [in the tractate]? One can answer: Presumably he retracted in favor of his colleague:

Tosafot on Chullin 77a:7:1.hebrew: נתמסמס מהו - הא דאמר באלו טרפות (לעיל חולין נג:) "נתמסמס הבשר רואין אותו כאילו הוא אינו", היינו כגון בריאה ובגידין שהטרפות תלוי בהן; אבל הכא שהטרפות תלוי בעצם, אע"ג דנתמסמס הבשר, שמא עדיין מגין:
Tosafot on Chullin 77a:7:1.english: [If] it was decomposed, what is [the halakha] - That which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (above, Chullin 53b), "[If] the flesh decomposed, we view it as if it is not [there]," that is [referring to cases] such as the lung and the sinews, upon which the tereifa status depends; but here, where the tereifa status depends on the bone, even though the flesh decomposed, perhaps it still protects [the bone]:

Tosafot on Chullin 77a:9:1.hebrew: דקנה משכא דידיה - בקונטרס גרס בדלי"ת, ור"ח ור"ת גרסי ברי"ש; פי': רירים, ליחה שלו, שאז מדבק בו העור ומעלה בו ארוכה:
Tosafot on Chullin 77a:9:1.english: That its own skin takes hold [dekanei mishkha dideih] - In the Kuntres [Rashi], he reads [it] with a dalet, whereas Rabbeinu Ḥananel and Rabbeinu Tam read [it] with a resh [rekanei]; meaning: secretions, its moisture, for then the skin adheres to it and brings about healing on it:
